correctness.rationale: Every equilibrium with at least two agents excludes singleton occupied runs: moving a singleton to the vacancy immediately preceding the next occupied run yields one neighbor. Any longer occupied run supplies an interior zero-utility agent, which could profitably move to the boundary of a vacant run of length at least two, so vacancies are all isolated. Dimer states give every agent utility one, while in the isolated-vacancy family every zero-utility interior agent stays with two occupied neighbors after any jump, because no vacancy lies adjacent to an interior agent. Cyclic positive-composition counts, three-pattern intersection, and boundary cases give the theorem. The standalone checker exhaustively compared 131064 occupancy configurations for cycle lengths 3 through 16 with an independent literal move test and checked 600 larger samples. Finite checks do not constitute the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The complete all-population stability classification, exact existence threshold including an odd-population exclusion below two-thirds density, and full labeled-placement census resolve a natural tractable family inside a model with general existence difficulties. The binomial count has mathematical purpose as a random-placement reliability benchmark, and the two different occupancy-run mechanisms give a substantive structural explanation, rather than a routine renamed combinatorial identity.
